info.title: Skald API
info.description: A server has two addresses. `<public URL>`, the server setting `--public-url`, is where the CLI and devices reach it. `<web URL>`, the setting `--web-url`, by default the public URL, is where browsers sign in: the providers' callbacks, the pages a sign-in returns to, its cookies, the `Origin` its browser forms are taken from and the verification page.

get.summary: The account's devices as the web app shows them
get.description: Every device of the session's account, in the order they registered, each with its state by the server's checks (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Device checks"); no key or certificate. It is the server's word: `skald` checks devices against the account's pinned master key.

200.description: The account's devices.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

200.description: The master public key of the session's account, or `null` while it has none.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

put.description: The account's first device gives the master public key with its own certificate, issued by that key (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Linking a device"). The server takes them only while the account has no master key.

200.description: The master key and certificate the account took before, sent again: a retry after a lost answer.

201.description: Taken: the account's master key, and the certificate of its device.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`ProtocolProblem`), or the request is invalid: a malformed body; a certificate that fails the proof check, that the master key does not sign or that names an `issuer`; or one whose account, device, kind, keys or `name` differ from the device's registration on the session's account.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

409.description: The account has a master key, and this is not the master key and certificate it took.

post.description: The one personal space of the session's account, which owns it and stores its revision 1 (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Roster"). The first request creates it, named as docs/dev/architecture.md, "Membership", says. The request has no body.

200.description: The account's personal space, created by an earlier request.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

post.description: A device of the session's account stores a revocation of one of the account's devices (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Revocation"), as the bytes the server got. The server stores it only if it counts against the account's master key, the certificates the server holds and the revocations it stored before. Once stored, each device that checks 3 and 4 of "Device checks" revoke with the account's revocations has no certificate wherever the server checks one: its mailbox entries expire, its KeyPackages are deleted, its connections close and it gets no later entry.

200.description: The account has this revocation with these bytes: a retry after a lost answer.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`ProtocolProblem`), or the request is invalid: a malformed body; or the problem `https://skald.so/problems/invalid-revocation`, for bytes that do not decode as a `revocation` or a revocation that does not count for the session's account, such as one of another account, one whose signature does not verify with the key `signer` names, or one with `also` by a device.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

get.description: Every session of the web session's account that has not ended or expired, web and device sessions alike, newest first. A request with a device session lists nothing.

200.description: The account's sessions.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown, ended or expired one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

403.description: The problem `https://skald.so/problems/not-allowed`: the request's session is a device session; only a web session lists or ends the account's sessions.

post.description: Ends every session of the web session's account but itself at once, web and device sessions alike, as `DELETE /account/sessions/{session}` ends one. Only with a web session's cookie, from a page of the web URL: a request whose `Origin` is any other, or that has none, ends nothing.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown, ended or expired one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

403.description: The problem `https://skald.so/problems/not-allowed`: the request's session is a device session, or the request does not come from a page of the web URL. Nothing is ended.

delete.summary: End a session of the account
delete.description: Ends a session of the web session's account at once: every later request with it is refused, and its WebSocket connections close with the reason `session-ended`, on every instance. A web session's links in progress end with it. A device session's device, its keys and its certificate stay, as at `DELETE /session`. Only with a web session's cookie, from a page of the web URL: a request whose `Origin` is any other, or that has none, ends nothing.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: The session's ID, as `GET /account/sessions` lists it.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown, ended or expired one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

403.description: The problem `https://skald.so/problems/not-allowed`: the request's session is a device session, or the request does not come from a page of the web URL. Nothing is ended.

404.description: The problem `https://skald.so/problems/no-session`: the account has no such session, or it has ended or expired.

200.description: The sign-in methods of the session's account: each signs in to it.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

delete.summary: Remove a sign-in method of the account
delete.description: Removes a sign-in method of the web session's account, never its last one: of two removals at once that would leave none, one is refused. The web sessions it signed in end at once, as at `DELETE /account/sessions/{session}`; device sessions stay. The removed method reaches no account: its next sign-in signs up as a new account, or is refused while sign-up is closed, and another account may link it. Only with a web session's cookie, from a page of the web URL, and a sign-in more recent than the server setting `--link-sign-in-age`: anything else removes nothing.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: The method's ID, as `GET /account/sign-in-methods` lists it.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown, ended or expired one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

403.description: Nothing is removed. The problem `https://skald.so/problems/not-allowed`: the request's session is a device session, or the request does not come from a page of the web URL. The problem `https://skald.so/problems/sign-in-too-old`: the web session's sign-in is older than `--link-sign-in-age`; the person signs in again first.

404.description: The problem `https://skald.so/problems/no-sign-in-method`: the account has no such sign-in method.

409.description: The problem `https://skald.so/problems/last-sign-in-method`: it is the account's last sign-in method, which is never removed.

get.summary: The spaces the account owns and its devices, with their limits
get.description: The spaces the session's account owns and its devices, each counted as its limit counts it, with the limit while the server has its setting (docs/dev/architecture.md, "Cloud limits"). Asking creates no personal space.

200.description: The account's usage.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

put.description: Sets the username of the session's account, from a web or a device session. A refused username leaves the old one.

204.description: Set: the account has this username.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`ProtocolProblem`), or the request is invalid: a malformed body, or a username that is not a `name` of an agent address.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

409.description: The username is reserved, or another account has it.

post.description: Device authorization (RFC 8628, §3.1): a machine without a browser asks for a device code and a user code. Its person approves the user code on the verification page, `GET /device`, within `expires_in` seconds, the server setting `--device-code-lifetime`; the machine meanwhile polls `POST /auth/token` every `interval` seconds, the server setting `--device-poll-interval`.

200.description: A new device code and its user code.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`application/problem+json`), or the request (`application/json`, RFC 6749, §5.2): `invalid_request` without a `client_id` or with one twice, `invalid_client` with another `client_id`.

404.description: Sign-in is off: the server has no sign-in settings.

get.description: Opened by the browser. Sends it to GitHub's authorization page, asking for no scope, with a `state` that the cookie this response sets binds to this browser and an S256 PKCE challenge of this sign-in. The `state` works once, until it expires; its lifetime is the server setting `--sign-in-state-lifetime`.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: The page of the web URL to return to once signed in: a path such as `/settings?tab=devices`, or its full address. Anything else, such as another site's address or the public URL's, returns to `/` of the web URL.

Location.description: GitHub's authorization page with the app's client ID, the callback `<web URL>/auth/github/callback`, `state`, `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256`.

Set-Cookie.description: The cookie that binds `state` to this browser: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` under an https web URL, for the callback's path only.

404.description: GitHub sign-in is off: the server has no GitHub settings.

get.description: Opened by the browser on its way back from GitHub. Checks `state` against the browser's cookie, exchanges `code` with the app's client ID and secret and the sign-in's PKCE verifier and reads the GitHub user. The first sign-in of a GitHub user creates an account with the user's GitHub ID as its GitHub sign-in method; later ones reach the account that holds that method and update the method's GitHub login. While the server's sign-up is closed, a first sign-in creates an account only for a GitHub login on the server's list, compared without case; the GitHub user's email does not count. Keeps no GitHub token. For a link, started by `POST /auth/github/link`, it adds the GitHub sign-in method to the account of the web session that started the link instead of signing in.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: GitHub's error, such as `access_denied`, instead of a code.

200.description: Signed in or linked: a page that sends the browser to the return page. For a link whose request lacks the cookie of the web session that started it, as one from another site lacks the `SameSite=Strict` cookie, first, once, a page that opens this callback again from this server.

Set-Cookie.description: Signed in: the session cookie `skald_session`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` under an https web URL; signed in or linked: the removal of the cookie that bound `state`.

400.description: No one is signed in, or nothing is linked: `state` is missing, wrong, from another browser, expired or used, also by the end of the web session that started a link, or GitHub gave no code or refused it.

403.description: A link that links nothing: the browser is not under the web session that started it, or that session ended during the callback. Or a refused sign-up: the server's sign-up is closed and the person, who has no account, is on none of its lists; the page names the problem type `https://skald.so/problems/sign-up-closed`, and nothing is created. A sign-in from the verification page with a user code refuses that code too: its polls answer `sign_up_closed`.

404.description: GitHub sign-in is off: the server has no GitHub settings.

409.description: A link that links nothing: another account has this GitHub sign-in method. Accounts never merge or move a method.

500.description: No one is signed in, or nothing is linked: the database failed.

502.description: No one is signed in, or nothing is linked: GitHub failed or refused the app's client ID and secret.

post.summary: Start a link of a GitHub sign-in method
post.description: Submitted by a form of a page of the web URL, such as `GET /sign-in-methods`, with the web session's cookie: a request whose `Origin` is any other, or that has none, links nothing. The web session's sign-in has to be more recent than the server setting `--link-sign-in-age`. Sends the browser to GitHub as `GET /auth/github` does, with a `state` that also binds the link to this web session; GitHub comes back through `GET /auth/github/callback`. The link works only while the session lasts.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: The page of the web URL the link returns to, as `return_to` of `GET /auth/github` names it; by default `GET /sign-in-methods`. Anything else, such as another site's address, returns to `/` of the web URL.

Location.description: GitHub's authorization page, as `GET /auth/github` sends the browser to.

Set-Cookie.description: The cookie that binds `state` to this browser, as `GET /auth/github` sets it.

403.description: Nothing is linked: the request has no web session, comes from another site, or its session's sign-in is older than `--link-sign-in-age`: then a page that asks to sign in again.

404.description: GitHub sign-in is off: the server has no GitHub settings.

get.description: Opened by the browser. Sends it to Google's authorization endpoint, by OpenID Connect's authorization code flow, asking for the scopes `openid` and `email` only, with a `state` that the cookie this response sets binds to this browser and a `nonce` and an S256 PKCE challenge of this sign-in. The `state` works once, until it expires; its lifetime is the server setting `--sign-in-state-lifetime`. The server reads Google's metadata from its issuer, the setting `--google-issuer`, at the first sign-in start that reaches it.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: The page of the web URL to return to once signed in: a path such as `/settings?tab=devices`, or its full address. Anything else, such as another site's address or the public URL's, returns to `/` of the web URL.

Location.description: Google's authorization endpoint with the client ID, the redirect URI `<web URL>/auth/google/callback`, `response_type=code`, the scopes `openid email`, `state`, `nonce`, `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256`.

Set-Cookie.description: The cookie that binds `state` to this browser: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` under an https web URL, for the callback's path only.

404.description: Google sign-in is off: the server has no Google settings.

502.description: Google is unreachable, or its metadata or keys are malformed.

get.description: Opened by the browser on its way back from Google. Checks `state` against the browser's cookie, exchanges `code` with the client ID and secret and the sign-in's PKCE verifier, and checks the ID token as OpenID Connect Core 1.0, §3.1.3.7, says, with this sign-in's `nonce`. The account is bound to its Google sign-in method, Google's issuer and the ID token's `sub`, never to the email. The first sign-in creates the account, its username made from the email's local part; later ones reach the account that holds that method, also after the email changes. While the server's sign-up is closed, a first sign-in creates an account only for an email on the server's list whose `email_verified` is true, or for an ID token whose `hd`, the Google Workspace or Cloud organization, is on its domain list; the email's domain does not count. Lists compare without case. Keeps no email, ID token or Google token. For a link, started by `POST /auth/google/link`, it adds the Google sign-in method to the account of the web session that started the link instead of signing in.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Google's error, such as `access_denied`, instead of a code.

200.description: Signed in or linked: a page that sends the browser to the return page. For a link whose request lacks the cookie of the web session that started it, as one from another site lacks the `SameSite=Strict` cookie, first, once, a page that opens this callback again from this server.

Set-Cookie.description: Signed in: the session cookie `skald_session`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` under an https web URL; signed in or linked: the removal of the cookie that bound `state`.

400.description: No one is signed in, or nothing is linked: `state` is missing, wrong, from another browser, expired or used, also by the end of the web session that started a link; or Google gave an error or no code, refused the code, or gave an ID token that fails a check, such as one with another sign-in's `nonce`.

403.description: A link that links nothing: the browser is not under the web session that started it, or that session ended during the callback. Or a refused sign-up: the server's sign-up is closed and the person, who has no account, is on none of its lists; the page names the problem type `https://skald.so/problems/sign-up-closed`, and nothing is created. A sign-in from the verification page with a user code refuses that code too: its polls answer `sign_up_closed`.

404.description: Google sign-in is off: the server has no Google settings.

409.description: A link that links nothing: another account has this Google sign-in method. Accounts never merge or move a method.

500.description: No one is signed in, or nothing is linked: the database failed.

502.description: No one is signed in, or nothing is linked: Google failed, is unreachable or refused the client ID and secret.

post.summary: Start a link of a Google sign-in method
post.description: Starts a link as `POST /auth/github/link` does, with Google: sends the browser to Google as `GET /auth/google` does, with `prompt=select_account`, so that the person chooses the Google account; Google comes back through `GET /auth/google/callback`.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: The page of the web URL the link returns to, as for `POST /auth/github/link`.

Location.description: Google's authorization page, as `GET /auth/google` sends the browser to, with `prompt=select_account`, so that the person chooses the Google account.

Set-Cookie.description: The cookie that binds `state` to this browser, as `GET /auth/google` sets it.

403.description: Nothing is linked: the request has no web session, comes from another site, or its session's sign-in is older than `--link-sign-in-age`: then a page that asks to sign in again.

404.description: Google sign-in is off: the server has no Google settings.

502.description: Google is unreachable, or its metadata or keys are malformed.

get.description: Needs no session. Names the providers the server has settings for and whether its sign-up is open, and nothing of the lists of who may sign up while it is closed.

200.description: The server's sign-in providers and sign-up.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

post.summary: Poll for a device flow's session token
post.description: The token endpoint (RFC 8628, §3.4): the machine polls with its device code, at most once per `interval` seconds, until its person approves or denies the user code, the server refuses its person's sign-up or the codes expire. An approved code gives a session token once; every later poll for it answers `invalid_grant`.

200.description: The person approved the user code: the session token for their account.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`application/problem+json`), or gives no token (`application/json`, RFC 8628, §3.5): `authorization_pending` until the person decides; `slow_down` to a poll that comes over 1 second sooner than `interval` seconds after the previous one, the server allowing 1 second of clock error; `access_denied` once the person denied the code; `sign_up_closed`, this server's own, once a sign-in from the verification page with the user code was refused as a sign-up, as sign-up is closed on the server, with `error_description` saying so; `expired_token` once the codes expired; `invalid_grant` for an unknown device code or one that already gave its token; `invalid_request`, `invalid_client` or `unsupported_grant_type` for a malformed request.

404.description: Sign-in is off: the server has no sign-in settings.

get.description: Opened by the person's browser at `verification_uri` or `verification_uri_complete`. It works while the server has the settings of any provider. With a web session, whatever sign-in method started it, it names the account's username, says that approving signs a machine in to that account and asks for the user code, filled in from `user_code`, with the buttons Approve and Deny, which submit `POST /device`. Opening it decides nothing.

parameters.name: user_code
parameters.description: The user code to fill in.

200.description: The page that asks for the code; without a web session, a link to sign in with each provider the server has settings for, GitHub or Google, each returning to this page with `user_code`.

404.description: Sign-in is off: the server has no sign-in settings.

post.summary: Approve or deny a user code
post.description: Submitted by the verification page's form, with the web session's cookie, from a page of the web URL: a request whose `Origin` is any other, or that has none, decides nothing. Approving binds the code to the session's account; a user code works once, for one account. After 10 wrong, used or expired codes within 15 minutes, the account's codes, right ones included, are refused until fewer remain in that window.

200.description: Approved or denied.

400.description: The code is wrong, used or expired, or the form has no decision.

403.description: The request has no web session, or comes from another site.

404.description: Sign-in is off: the server has no sign-in settings.

429.description: Too many wrong codes: the account's codes are refused for a while.

200.description: The devices of the session's account, each with its certificate as the device sent it, or `null` while it has none, and the account's revocations.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

post.description: A new device registers its ID and public keys with its account (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Linking a device"). Only `client` devices register here.

200.description: The same registration again, by the same account: a retry after a lost answer.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`ProtocolProblem`), or the registration is invalid: a malformed body, an ID not derived from `signing`, a kind other than `client`, a key not of 32 bytes or a `name` not of 1 to 64 bytes.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

403.description: The problem `https://skald.so/problems/devices-limit`: a new device of an account that has as many devices with a certificate as the server setting `--devices-limit` allows. Devices without a certificate, `service` devices and revoked devices do not count. Without the setting there is no limit.

409.description: The server has the ID with other keys or `name`, or on another account.

get.description: How many unused KeyPackages a device of the session's account has, and whether its last-resort one is to be replaced (docs/protocol/membership.md, "KeyPackages"). The server deletes expired ones first.

200.description: The device's KeyPackages: how many unused ones expire in more than 7 days, and whether its last-resort one is to be replaced.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

404.description: The problem `https://skald.so/problems/no-device`: the session's account has no such device.

post.description: Takes KeyPackages of a `client` device of the session's account with a certificate, not revoked, and its last-resort one, which replaces the one it had (docs/protocol/membership.md, "KeyPackages"). Each must pass the checks a device runs before it adds one: its MLS signatures verify, its lifetime holds and spans at most 60 days, its ciphersuite is `0x0001`, and its `identity` and `signature_key` are the device's; the last-resort one also carries the `last_resort` extension. One that fails refuses them all. The same KeyPackage again is stored once.

200.description: Taken: the device's KeyPackages after the upload.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`ProtocolProblem`), or the upload is invalid: a malformed body, or the problem `https://skald.so/problems/invalid-key-package`, a KeyPackage that fails the checks.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

403.description: The device is not a `client` device with a certificate, or is revoked, or it would hold more than 100 unused KeyPackages.

404.description: The problem `https://skald.so/problems/no-device`: the session's account has no such device.

200.description: The server is up and PostgreSQL answers.

post.description: Hands out one KeyPackage of each device asked for that is a `client` device with a certificate, not revoked, of an account that shares a space with the session's (docs/protocol/membership.md, "KeyPackages"): another one, which the server then deletes, or, once none is left, the device's last-resort one, which it keeps. No expired one, and no KeyPackage to two requests.

200.description: The KeyPackages handed out, at most one per device; a device with none for the session is left out.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`ProtocolProblem`), or the request is invalid: a malformed body or a device ID that is not one.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>`.

post.description: Deletes the entries of the device's mailbox up to `seq`, as `ack` on a WebSocket does (docs/protocol/delivery.md, "Mailbox").

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`ProtocolProblem`), or the request is invalid (`https://skald.so/problems/invalid-request`): a body that is not the operation's frame, or a missing or invalid parameter.

401.description: The request is not proved, and the server reads, acks and stores nothing: `not-signed-in` for no device session of the bearer token, such as an ended one; otherwise the reason a WebSocket's `auth` is refused for (docs/protocol/delivery.md, "Connecting"): `auth-required` without a valid `Skald-Device-Proof`, `challenge-refused`, `device-refused` or `signature-refused`.

413.description: The body is over 64 MiB, the longest a WebSocket message may be.

get.description: Server-sent events (docs/protocol/delivery.md, "Frames" and "Mailbox"). Acks the device's mailbox up to the cursor in `Last-Event-ID`, then sends the entries after it in `seq` order, then an empty `batch` once it has sent every entry the mailbox held at the opening, then each new entry and `space-notice`, through any instance. Each event's `data` is one frame, its CBOR in base64url without padding; the `id` of a `message` or `status` event is its `seq`. While idle, the stream sends a comment line at the interval of the server setting `--sse-keep-alive`. It ends when its session ends or its device is revoked. The device sends and acks with `POST /mailbox/send` and `POST /mailbox/ack`.

200.description: The stream.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`ProtocolProblem`), or the request is invalid (`https://skald.so/problems/invalid-request`): a `Last-Event-ID` that is not a `seq`.

401.description: The stream is not proved, and the server reads and acks nothing: `not-signed-in` for no device session of the bearer token, such as an ended one; otherwise the reason a WebSocket's `auth` is refused for (docs/protocol/delivery.md, "Connecting"): `auth-required` without a valid `Skald-Device-Proof`, `challenge-refused`, `device-refused` or `signature-refused`.

post.description: Acks the device's mailbox up to the `sync` frame's cursor and answers a `batch` of the entries after it, in `seq` order, and a `space-notice` for each space with a roster revision stored since the device's previous long-poll answer (docs/protocol/delivery.md, "Mailbox"). It answers at once when it has some or `wait` is 0; otherwise with the first to come within `wait`, through any instance, or an empty `batch` at its end. A waiting long-poll whose session ends or whose device is revoked ends with `401`, as a new request would.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: How long to wait for something to answer, in seconds; the server waits at most its setting `--long-poll-max-wait`.

200.description: A `batch` frame.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`ProtocolProblem`), or the request is invalid (`https://skald.so/problems/invalid-request`): a body that is not the operation's frame, or a missing or invalid parameter.

401.description: The request is not proved, and the server reads, acks and stores nothing: `not-signed-in` for no device session of the bearer token, such as an ended one; otherwise the reason a WebSocket's `auth` is refused for (docs/protocol/delivery.md, "Connecting"): `auth-required` without a valid `Skald-Device-Proof`, `challenge-refused`, `device-refused` or `signature-refused`.

413.description: The body is over 64 MiB, the longest a WebSocket message may be.

post.description: A device that keeps no WebSocket sends an envelope, as `send` on a WebSocket does (docs/protocol/delivery.md, "Send"): the same answers, idempotency and order.

200.description: The `stored` or `send-refused` frame.

Only a session of the space's creator stores revision 1, which lists that account as an admin; only a session of an admin in revision n stores revision n+1. Its `signer` is a device of the session's account with a certificate on the server.

get.description: Opens a WebSocket (RFC 6455) after checking the protocol version the request states, as docs/protocol/README.md, "Server answers", says. Its first frame, `auth`, proves the connection's device on a challenge of `POST /session/challenge` (docs/protocol/delivery.md, "Connecting"); a connection without a valid proof is closed as "Connecting" there says. The server then answers each `send` with `stored` or `send-refused` ("Send" there) and, from the connection's first `sync`, sends its device's mailbox ("Mailbox" there). Once the server stores a roster revision, it sends `space-notice` on each connection of a device of an account the revision lists ("Frames" there).

DeviceProof.description: The device's proof (docs/protocol/delivery.md, "Connecting"): the CBOR `[challenge: bstr, device: id, signature: bstr .size 64]` in base64url without padding. `challenge` is a challenge of the bearer token's session from `POST /session/challenge`, which works once; `signature` signs `["skald request", challenge, origin]`.

ProtocolVersion.name: Skald-Protocol-Version
ProtocolVersion.description: The protocol version the request states.

NoStore.description: `no-store`: the response holds a sign-in's codes, token or outcome.

session.description: The web session that a sign-in in the browser gives, with GitHub or Google.

bearer.description: The session token that the device flow gives: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

AccountUsage.description: The spaces an account owns and its devices, each with its limit while one applies.

devices.description: The account's devices with a certificate, `service` and revoked devices aside, as `--devices-limit` counts them; the limit is its value.

Certificate.description: A device certificate's CBOR bytes (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Device certificate") in base64url without padding (RFC 4648, §5).

challenge.description: 32 random bytes in base64url without padding (RFC 4648, §5).

group.description: Whether the channel has an MLS group: the server kept its first Commit.

group_info.description: The GroupInfo of the current epoch; `null` while the server has none.

cert.description: The certificate as the device sent it; `null` while it has none.

device_code.description: The secret the machine polls with.

user_code.description: The code the person types: 8 letters from `BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXZ` as `XXXX-XXXX`. The verification page ignores case and every character but letters and digits.

verification_uri_complete.description: The verification page with the user code filled in: `<web URL>/device?user_code=<user code>`.

interval.description: The least number of seconds between polls.

user_code.description: The user code as the person typed it.

DeviceId.description: A device's ID: a UUIDv8 derived from its signing key, in the lowercase hyphenated form (docs/protocol/README.md, "Identifiers").

signing.description: The Ed25519 public key the ID derives from.

name.description: 1 to 64 bytes of UTF-8, set on the device; its certificate's `name`.

access_token.description: The session token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

revocations.description: The stored revocations of the listed devices' accounts, each as the server got it, once.

Frame.description: A frame of docs/protocol/delivery.md, "Frames": one CBOR item.

GroupInfo.description: A channel's GroupInfo in an `MLSMessage` (RFC 9420, §6), with the `ratchet_tree` and `external_pub` extensions (docs/protocol/membership.md, "MLS profile"), in base64url without padding (RFC 4648, §5).

items.description: An encoded `history-entry` (docs/protocol/membership.md, "History entry"), in base64url without padding (RFC 4648, §5).
An encoded `history-link` (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Key chain"), in base64url without padding (RFC 4648, §5).
An encoded `history-wrap` (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Wraps"), in base64url without padding (RFC 4648, §5).

KeyPackage.description: A KeyPackage in an `MLSMessage` (RFC 9420, §6 and §10) in base64url without padding (RFC 4648, §5).

unused.description: The device's unused KeyPackages, the last-resort one aside, that expire in more than 7 days.

replace_last_resort.description: Whether the device has no last-resort KeyPackage, or one that was handed out or expires within 7 days.

KeyPackageUpload.description: Either field may be left out.

ListedDevice.description: A device of the account as the web app shows it: no key or certificate.

name.description: The name the device registered with.

kind.description: The device's kind, as it registered.

state.description: By checks 3 and 4 of docs/protocol/membership.md, "Device checks", with the account's stored revocations: `linked`, a device with a certificate they do not revoke; `waiting`, a device with no certificate yet, waiting for linking; `revoked`, a device they revoke, as one certified by a revoked device.

ListedMember.description: A member of a space as the web app shows it: no key.

handle.description: The member's handle in the revision.

role.description: The member's role in the revision.

github_login.description: The GitHub login of the account's GitHub method; absent while it has none, or when this server does not hold the account.

linked_devices.description: How many of the account's devices `GET /account/devices` gives as `linked`.

joined_at.description: When the server stored the revision that added the member, after which every revision lists it.

ListedSession.description: A session of the account: a web session, from a sign-in in the browser, or a device session, from the device flow. No IP address or location.

kind.description: `web` for a web session, `device` for a device session.

browser.description: A web session's browser, as the `User-Agent` of its sign-in names it, such as `Chrome`; only when it names a known one.

os.description: A web session's operating system, as the `User-Agent` of its sign-in names it, such as `macOS`; only when it names a known one.

device_name.description: The name of the device a device session last registered or connected as; only once it has.

last_used_at.description: The session's last request, to the minute: a request records its use only when the last one is a minute old or more.

expires_at.description: When a web session expires: 30 days after its sign-in, its cookie with it. The server then refuses it as an ended one and lists it no more. Only for a web session: a device session lasts until it ends.

current.description: Whether it is the request's own session.

ListedSpace.description: A space of the account's spaces list.

personal.description: Whether it is the personal space of the session's account; another account's personal space is not.

master.description: The account's master public key; `null` while it has none.

cert.description: The certificate of the device, issued by the master key.

OwnedSpaces.description: The spaces an account owns, as `--owned-spaces-limit` counts them: the ones it created, its personal space included also before it is created. `spaces` lists those that exist.

limit.description: The value of `--owned-spaces-limit`; absent without it.

ProtocolProblem.description: A problem details object (RFC 9457) that refuses the stated protocol version.

PublicKey.description: An Ed25519 or X25519 public key: 32 bytes in base64url without padding (RFC 4648, §5).

Revocation.description: A revocation's CBOR bytes (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Revocation") in base64url without padding (RFC 4648, §5).

RosterRevision.description: A roster revision's CBOR bytes (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Roster") in base64url without padding (RFC 4648, §5).

name.description: The server's name; `null` without a valid one, such as with no public address or an IP address as its host.

github_login.description: The GitHub login of the account's GitHub sign-in method as of its latest sign-in, for display; only while the account has one.

sign_in_method.description: The provider a web session signed in with; only for a web session.

provider.description: `github`, or `google` for the server's OIDC provider.

github_login.description: A GitHub method's GitHub login as of its latest sign-in, for display; only for GitHub.

sign_up.description: `open`: a first sign-in creates an account. `closed`: only for the people the server lists.

message_size.description: The longest payload of an envelope, in bytes: the value of `--message-size-limit`.

mailbox_retention.description: How long an undelivered message waits at most, in seconds: the value of `--mailbox-retention`.
